page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at a 5.0 GHz clock speed. System memory consists of 4.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM rated at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded performance contrasted with low total throughput due to the single-core configuration. The instance reaches the top tier in Geekbench single-core scoring (3084.0), stress-ng single-core execution (4180.09), single-threaded gzip compression (45.72 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (20.29 GB/sec). Geekbench text processing also lands in the top decile. Conversely, aggregate metrics reflecting multi-threaded parallel throughput, such as multi-core Geekbench (3068.0), PassMark CPU score (3871.4), and Redis SET operations (4.76 million operations/sec), register in the lower percentiles because of the single available thread.

From an efficiency standpoint, the m8azn.medium offers an entry-level deployment profile that minimizes resource commitment while maximizing per-core instruction velocity. Because there is only 1 vCPU and no local NVMe storage, workloads demanding multi-threaded parallelism or heavy sustained local I/O will face operational bottlenecks. It is best matched for single-threaded batch tasks, lightweight microservices, single-worker background queues, low-traffic web serving, and small-model text generation where peak single-core speed is prioritized over core density.

Backed by instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, the instance excels in single-threaded tasks, recording top-tier benchmark results in Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression.
